articles.title: Survival and Risk Factors of Implants Placed in Sites of Previous Failures-A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.summary: In 177,410 implants across 59,238 patients, survival fell from 97.6% for first implants at a site to 92.2% for second (HR 4.60) and 88.5% for third or later placements (HR 5.71). Replacement implants at a previously failed site carry a substantially higher failure risk that should be quantified during consent and may justify site preparation or an alternative plan.
articles.bottom_line: Explicitly warn patients that a replacement implant at a failed site has roughly 4–6 times the failure hazard, and consider grafting or alternative restorative options.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes of 6-mm Short Implants Supporting Splinted Crowns in Posterior Regions: A 12-Year Prospective Multi-Centre Single-Cohort Study.
articles.summary: In 45 patients with 95 splinted 6-mm implants in posterior sites, 12-year cumulative survival was 92.6% with essentially no marginal bone loss (-0.09 mm), though peri-implant mucositis affected 37.8% of implants and peri-implantitis 2.7%. This is the longest prospective follow-up supporting short splinted implants as a durable alternative to bone augmentation in atrophic posterior ridges.
articles.bottom_line: Offer splinted 6-mm implants with confidence in the resorbed posterior jaw instead of routine vertical augmentation.

articles.title: Clinical, Radiographic and Patient-Centred Outcomes of MINST Versus MIST With Enamel Matrix Derivative in Class II Mandibular Furcation Defects: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.summary: In 40 patients with mandibular Class II furcations, flapless MINST with enamel matrix derivative was non-inferior to MIST + EMD at 9 months (PPD reduction 2.15 vs 2.20 mm; adjusted difference -0.22 mm). A non-surgical approach may achieve comparable furcation outcomes with better patient-reported experience.
articles.bottom_line: Consider flapless MINST with EMD as a first-line alternative to flap surgery for Class II mandibular furcations, pending longer-term confirmation.

articles.title: Long-Term Incidence of Peri-Implant Conditions: 25-Year Results of The Bernese Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Clinical implant dentistry and related research
articles.summary: In the Bernese prospective cohort, tissue-level implant survival was 98.8% at 10 years and 94.0% at 25 years, with peri-implantitis rising from 3.5% to 9.1% at implant level while mucositis stayed high (76.5%) and only 14.4% of implants remained fully healthy. Long-term implant survival is excellent but peri-implant mucosal health is the exception, not the rule.
articles.bottom_line: Quote ~94% 25-year survival to patients while enrolling every implant patient in lifelong peri-implant maintenance.

articles.title: Protective factors and critical mucosal thickness for the stability of the peri-implant soft tissue margin over 5 years: A longitudinal cohort study.
articles.summary: In 133 anterior single implants followed 5 years, mucosal thickness at 3 mm apical to the margin was the critical determinant of soft tissue margin stability, with a threshold of ≥2.23 mm associated with long-term stability. This gives a concrete, measurable soft-tissue thickness target for anterior implant planning and grafting decisions.
articles.bottom_line: Aim for ≥2.2 mm mucosal thickness apical to the margin at anterior implants, grafting soft tissue when it falls short.

articles.title: Management of pain with oral analgesia after extraction of lower third molars: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery
articles.summary: A network meta-analysis of 19 RCTs and 3615 third molar surgeries ranked opioid plus NSAID combinations as the most effective single-dose analgesic strategy for 6-hour total pain relief, with NSAIDs alone next best and all active drugs beating placebo. This supports NSAIDs as the default first-line agent, with an opioid added only when pain is expected to be severe.
articles.bottom_line: Prescribe an NSAID as baseline post-extraction analgesia and reserve NSAID-opioid combinations for anticipated severe pain.

articles.title: Surgical Therapy for Peri-Implantitis Using Deproteinised Bovine Bone Mineral With 10% Collagen, Enamel Matrix Derivative and Doxycycline: A Prospective Cohort 10-Year Implant Study.
articles.summary: Ten-year follow-up of 30 reconstructively treated peri-implantitis cases showed 96.6% implant survival, probing depth falling from 8.9 to 3.1 mm and radiographic bone loss from 57% to 13% using EDTA decontamination plus DBBM-collagen/EMD/doxycycline with strict maintenance. Long-term data of this length are rare and support reconstructive surgery in compliant non-smokers with rigorous supportive therapy.
articles.bottom_line: Offer reconstructive peri-implantitis surgery with this protocol to selected non-smoking, periodontally stable patients, but commit them to lifelong supportive peri-implant care.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of free gingival graft, xenogeneic collagen matrix, and acellular dermal matrix for peri-implant keratinized mucosa augmentation: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: In 44 implants with KMW <2 mm, free gingival graft with apically positioned flap gave significantly greater 12-month buccal soft-tissue volume (+24.1 mm³) than acellular dermal matrix (-17.3 mm³), with xenogeneic matrix intermediate and no significant KMW difference between groups. Substitutes can widen keratinized mucosa but only autogenous FGG reliably adds volume.
articles.bottom_line: Use autogenous FGG when peri-implant tissue volume as well as keratinized width is needed; substitutes suffice if width alone is the goal.

articles.title: Association between implant adjacency and survival of endodontically treated teeth.
articles.summary: In 787 patients, endodontically treated teeth adjacent to implants survived far shorter (44-56 months vs 85-127 months) and had nearly nine-fold higher odds of loss from vertical root fracture (aOR 8.90), with posts adding risk. Placing an implant next to a root-filled tooth may put that tooth at substantial fracture risk.
articles.bottom_line: Warn patients and consider cuspal-coverage protection when an endodontically treated tooth neighbours a planned implant.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Periodontal Regenerative Therapy Utilizing the Double-Sided Entire Papilla Preservation (DEPP) Technique for Infrabony Defects: A 12-Month Follow-up Case Series.
articles.journal: The International journal of periodontics & restorative dentistry
articles.summary: A case series using the double-sided entire papilla preservation flap with growth factor or enamel matrix derivative plus a bone substitute reported mean probing depth reduction of 5.0 mm and clinical attachment gain of 5.3 mm at 12 months in infrabony defects extending palatally. The magnitude of gain suggests the technique is a useful option for defects that cannot be accessed from the buccal alone.
articles.bottom_line: Add DEPP to your flap repertoire for palatally extending infrabony defects, pending controlled comparison.

articles.title: Treatment of External Cervical Resorption via Surgical Crown Lengthening and Concomitant Placement of a Resin-Modified Glass-Ionomer Restoration: A Case Series with 1- to 4-Year Follow-up.
articles.journal: The International journal of periodontics & restorative dentistry
articles.summary: Ten external cervical resorption lesions treated by surgical crown lengthening with simultaneous resin-modified glass-ionomer restoration showed high tooth survival over 1-4 years of follow-up. It offers a reproducible, single-visit surgical-restorative protocol for a lesion periodontists are often asked to manage.
articles.bottom_line: Consider crown lengthening with concurrent RMGI restoration as a predictable option for accessible external cervical resorption lesions.

articles.title: Extensive Cervicofacial and Mediastinal Emphysema Following Subgingival Air-Polishing for Peri-Implantitis: A Case Report.
articles.summary: A 32-year-old developed extensive cervicofacial and mediastinal emphysema after subgingival erythritol air-polishing of a peri-implantitis site with a 6-mm pocket and a labial sinus tract, requiring hospital admission though he remained stable. It flags a specific and avoidable risk of a device many periodontists use weekly.
articles.bottom_line: Avoid subgingival air-polishing at implant sites with a sinus tract or breached soft tissue, and warn patients about emphysema signs.
